subject: Throughput vs. Latency — budget check-in and tier preference
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acmeai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput vs. Latency — budget check-in and tier preference

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can align on the pilot configuration:

Summary from the call:
- AcmeAI target workload: search & chat for knowledge base (mixed short/long contexts). Estimated monthly tokens: 80M–200M (early pilot -> scale).
- Latency SLO goal: 95th <= 350ms for chat UX; some batch reranking can accept 700–1,200ms.
- Budget: ACV target range we discussed was $60k–$150k/year for pilot to POC (you said procurement expects a two-tier budget).

Questions / asks (next steps):
1) Can you confirm a target $/1M tokens target for the pilot — you mentioned aiming for roughly $350–$900 per 1M tokens depending on tier.
2) Priority vs Standard tier: you indicated preference for lower latency for the chat path; do you want to commit to a small Priority allocation (eg. 2 GPUs) for chat and Standard for reranking?
3) We'll attach a short profile template (csv) for traffic shape — please return with 1–2 representative days.

Quick recommendation (from our side):
- If you need consistent 95th <= 350ms for interactive chat, we suggest a mixed routing: Priority for chat (streaming enabled, minimal batching) + Standard for batch reranks (aggressive batching, higher throughput). This typically lands unit economics in the $400–$700 / 1M tokens band for your volume profile.

I've attached the profile template and a draft pricing sheet to make the math explicit.

Proposed next steps:
- Sam: send back sample traffic profile and confirm target $/1M tokens band.
- Aditya: share estimated POC config (GPU count, expected latency/bandwidth) once we get traffic.
- Marissa: prep a one-page pilot SOW with two options (Priority-light vs Priority-heavy).

Thanks — happy to hop back on a 20-min call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_poc_profile.csv (template), redwood_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing summary)
From: Sam Patel <sam@acmeai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:01:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Throughput vs. Latency — budget check-in and tier preference

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tokens: our best guess for the pilot month is ~120M tokens (combined prompts + generations). If the pilot progresses to production, we expect to move toward the upper range ~300–500M over 6–9 months.
- Budget: the $60k–$150k/year range is correct; procurement will push for the lower half, but we can structure as a phased commit if performance looks good.
- $/1M target: internally, we'd like to see something at or below $500 / 1M tokens for the steady-state mix; for the initial pilot we can accept up to $750 / 1M if latency targets are met.

About tiers: we like the mixed approach. For the pilot please provision:
- Priority pool: enough to sustain ~60 concurrent interactive sessions (low-latency priority routing, streaming on).
- Standard pool: for reranking and batch tasks — we can accept higher latency there.

I'll attach a day-of-traffic sample by EOD tomorrow. Also cc'ing our infra lead (will add in the next thread) if we need deeper networking/security questions.

Sam
Head of Product
AcmeAI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acmeai.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput vs. Latency — pilot sizing and cost estimate

On Mon, 10 May 2027 at 09:01, Sam Patel <sam@acmeai.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
> - Tokens: ~120M pilot month, scale to 300–500M.
> - Budget: target <= $500 / 1M steady; pilot up to $750 / 1M.
>
Thanks Sam — quick technical/price sketch below so you have numbers to share with procurement. This is a conservative estimate based on the mixed routing you requested.

Pilot assumptions:
- Pilot month volume: 120M tokens
- Chat interactive path: ~35% of tokens, target 95th P50 latency goal < 350ms. We allocate a small Priority pool (equivalent of 2x A100-like GPUs) with streaming enabled and low batching (batch size <= 8 typical).
- Rerank/batch path: ~65% of tokens, standard pool with batching (batch sizes 64–128), higher throughput tolerance (95th up to 1,200ms).

Estimated unit economics (approx):
- Priority interactive path: $820 / 1M tokens (pilot, low batching + streaming overhead).
- Standard batch path: $320 / 1M tokens (high batching benefits).
- Blended pilot rate (approx): (0.35*820 + 0.65*320) = ~$490 / 1M tokens.

If you move more volume into Standard and allow slightly higher chat latency (eg. 95th ~450ms with batching of 16), blended can come down to ~$380 / 1M. If you need consistent 95th <= 250ms, costs increase materially.

Recommendations / options for procurement:
- Option A (latency-first pilot): commit to small Priority reserve for chat. Blended ~ $480–$520 / 1M for pilot; demonstrates UX.
- Option B (cost-first pilot): keep chat in Standard with modest batching (accept 95th ~450ms); blended ~ $350–$400 / 1M.

I'll attach the quick calc and a sample SLO clause for the pilot. Also: we can include an automatic fallback policy — if Priority capacity saturates we burst to Standard with a stealth queue so users see graceful degradation, which helps control cost spikes.

Next steps from us:
- Once we get the traffic sample, I'll produce a GPU / throughput sizing sheet and a two-option pricing appendix for procurement.
- Marissa will draft a short SOW that includes the two pilot options.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing calc), acme_poc_profile.csv (sample filled by Aditya: day1.csv stub)
From: Sam Patel <sam@acmeai.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Throughput vs. Latency — budget check-in and tier preference

Thanks Aditya — that blended math is exactly what procurement needs. I'll do the following:
- Share a representative 48-hour traffic dump (anonymized) by EOD.
- For the pilot we'll start with Option A (latency-first) but request a clause to drop to Option B if usage remains below 200M after month 2.

One quick question: can you confirm whether the Priority pool supports per-request streaming (SSE) without degrading 95th P50 targets? We need streaming to power a typeahead-like UX.

If you can confirm streaming will be supported and included in the pilot SOW, we'll get procurement moving.

Sam
Head of Product, AcmeAI
